channel.title: KubeIntellect Blog
channel.description: Technical writing on LLM agents, AI SRE, and Kubernetes operations.

item.title: A Kubernetes AI agent should never say 'healthy' about pods it couldn't see
item.description: A one-line bug could make a truncated cluster listing look complete: on a 401-pod cluster, one CrashLoopBackOff sorted past an 8,000-character cap and the agent reported '85 pods, no issues.' The cause, why green tests missed it, and the fix.

item.title: KubeIntellect is peer-reviewed and open access — read the paper
item.description: The KubeIntellect framework is published in the Journal of Grid Computing (Springer, 2026) and is open access. 93% query resolution on a live cluster, +25 points over a raw GPT-4o baseline. Links to the DOI, ACM, and arXiv.

item.title: How to choose an AI tool for Kubernetes: the capabilities that matter
item.description: A capability-first guide to evaluating any AI tool for Kubernetes — the difference between look, explain, reason, and act — and where to draw the safety line.

item.title: When an AI agent hits a wall, it should write its own tool
item.description: How the KubeIntellect agent synthesizes, validates, and registers new Kubernetes tools at runtime — and the guardrails that make it safe. 81.8% success on novel requests, from the published evaluation.

item.title: Why more AI agents is not more capability
item.description: An honest engineering lesson from building an LLM operator for Kubernetes: going from the 13 specialized agents of the published v1 design to a lean coordinator made it better and cheaper. More agents is not more capability.
